title: When Numbers Change the Work
title_ja: 数字が仕事のあり方を変えるとき
fact_notes: 市役所、測定制度、関係者は架空の教育用事例。公共サービスの評価をめぐる論点を扱う独自教材。

sentences.en: A municipal service office introduced a performance system that rewarded employees for resolving the greatest number of requests each day.
sentences.ja: ある市役所の窓口は、一日に最も多くの相談案件を処理した職員を評価する業績制度を導入した。

sentences.en: Managers believed that clearer targets would reduce waiting times and help the office demonstrate responsible use of public money.
sentences.ja: 管理職は明確な目標によって待ち時間を減らし、公費の責任ある使用を示せると考えた。

sentences.en: Initially, the results appeared encouraging because the average number of completed cases increased and queues became shorter.
sentences.ja: 当初は処理済み案件の平均件数が増え、待ち行列も短くなったため、結果は有望に見えた。

sentences.en: However, several employees noticed that complex cases were becoming less attractive to handle because they required longer conversations.
sentences.ja: しかし複雑な案件は長い対話を要するため、担当したがられなくなっていると一部職員は気づいた。

sentences.en: A resident dealing with several connected difficulties might need careful guidance that could not be delivered within a standard appointment.
sentences.ja: 複数の関連する困難を抱える住民には、標準の面談時間では伝えきれない丁寧な助言が必要かもしれない。

sentences.en: The new measurements therefore raised a question about whether greater efficiency always meant better public service.
sentences.ja: そこで新しい測定基準は、効率の向上が常に公共サービスの改善を意味するのかという問いを生んだ。

sentences.en: Numbers have genuine advantages when organizations need to understand how limited resources are being used.
sentences.ja: 組織が限られた資源の使われ方を把握する必要があるとき、数字には実際の利点がある。

sentences.en: Without basic records, managers may overlook growing delays or fail to recognize that some offices are carrying unusually heavy workloads.
sentences.ja: 基本記録がなければ、管理職は遅延の増加を見落としたり、一部の窓口に異常に重い仕事量がかかっていると気づけなかったりする。

sentences.en: For example, counting unfinished applications can reveal a problem that individual workers have struggled to describe.
sentences.ja: 例えば未処理の申請を数えると、個々の職員が説明しにくかった問題が明らかになることがある。

sentences.en: Yet a measurement is always a selection of what can be counted, not a complete description of what matters.
sentences.ja: しかし測定とは常に数えられるものを選んだ結果であり、大切なことすべてを記述するものではない。

sentences.en: If a target ignores listening, employees may become reluctant to spend time explaining options to confused residents.
sentences.ja: 目標が傾聴を無視すれば、職員は戸惑う住民に選択肢を説明する時間を使いたがらなくなるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The challenge is to distinguish information that supports judgment from numbers that silently replace judgment.
sentences.ja: 課題は、判断を支える情報と、知らぬ間に判断そのものに取って代わる数字を区別することである。

sentences.en: One employee described helping an older resident who had submitted several forms containing conflicting information.
sentences.ja: ある職員は、矛盾する情報が書かれた複数の書類を提出した高齢の住民を支援した経験を話した。

sentences.en: Correcting the records required listening to the resident's account and contacting another department for clarification.
sentences.ja: 記録の訂正には、住民の話を聞き、別の部署に確認する必要があった。

sentences.en: Although the employee completed only one case that afternoon, the work prevented the resident from making repeated unnecessary visits.
sentences.ja: その職員は午後に一件しか処理できなかったが、住民が何度も無駄に訪問する事態を防げた。

sentences.en: Under the original system, this effort would have appeared less productive than completing several simple requests.
sentences.ja: 元の制度では、この努力は簡単な案件を何件も終えるより生産性が低いように見えただろう。

sentences.en: The example suggested that the quality of an outcome may depend on benefits extending beyond the period being measured.
sentences.ja: この例は、結果の質が測定期間を超えて生じる利益に依存する場合があると示した。

sentences.en: It also demonstrated why people closest to the work sometimes possess knowledge that distant administrators cannot easily observe.
sentences.ja: 仕事に最も近い人々が、遠くの管理者には観察しにくい知識を持つ理由も示していた。

sentences.en: Critics of the new targets argued that workers would eventually prioritize easy cases simply because they improved reported performance.
sentences.ja: 新しい目標の批判者は、職員が報告上の業績を上げるというだけの理由で簡単な案件を優先するようになると主張した。

sentences.en: Supporters responded that removing targets entirely could weaken accountability and make poor service difficult to identify.
sentences.ja: 一方支持者は、目標を完全になくせば説明責任が弱まり、質の低いサービスを見つけにくくなると反論した。

sentences.en: Both positions contained reasonable concerns, since public services must be responsive without wasting resources.
sentences.ja: 公共サービスは資源を無駄にせず住民に応えるべきなので、どちらの立場にも合理的な懸念があった。

sentences.en: Instead of abandoning measurement, the office decided to test a broader set of indicators and review them with employees.
sentences.ja: 測定をやめる代わりに、窓口はより広い指標を試し、職員とともに見直すことにした。

sentences.en: The revised approach considered unresolved problems, the need for follow-up appointments, and explanations of exceptional cases.
sentences.ja: 修正案では、未解決の問題、追加面談の必要性、例外的な案件についての説明を考慮した。

sentences.en: Managers also promised that no single indicator would automatically determine an employee's evaluation.
sentences.ja: 管理職はまた、ただ一つの指標で職員の評価が自動的に決まることはないと約束した。

sentences.en: The experiment quickly revealed that qualitative information could create its own difficulties if collected without clear rules.
sentences.ja: 実験は、質的な情報も明確な規則なしに集めれば独自の問題を生み得るとすぐに明らかにした。

sentences.en: Residents who received disappointing decisions might express dissatisfaction even when staff had explained the law accurately and respectfully.
sentences.ja: 望まない決定を受けた住民は、職員が法律を正確かつ丁寧に説明していても不満を表すかもしれない。

sentences.en: Conversely, a pleasant conversation was not proof that the advice given had been complete or correct.
sentences.ja: 逆に、感じのよい会話だったからといって、助言が完全で正しかった証拠にはならない。

sentences.en: The office therefore avoided treating satisfaction surveys as an unquestionable substitute for case counts.
sentences.ja: そこで窓口は、満足度調査を案件数に代わる絶対的な指標として扱うことを避けた。

sentences.en: It combined feedback with periodic case reviews, privacy safeguards, and opportunities for employees to explain unusual circumstances.
sentences.ja: 意見に加え、定期的な案件審査、プライバシー保護、職員が例外的な事情を説明する機会を組み合わせた。

sentences.en: The aim was not to create a perfect score but to expose the strengths and limitations of each source of information.
sentences.ja: 目的は完璧な点数を作ることではなく、情報源それぞれの長所と限界を明らかにすることだった。

sentences.en: During the review, managers discovered that some staff members had begun changing their behavior to satisfy the published targets.
sentences.ja: 見直しの中で管理職は、一部職員が公表された目標を満たすために行動を変え始めていたと気づいた。

sentences.en: They did not necessarily intend to deceive anyone, but the rules rewarded speed more clearly than careful problem-solving.
sentences.ja: 必ずしも誰かをだますつもりではなかったが、規則は丁寧な問題解決より速さを明確に評価していた。

sentences.en: For this reason, the office invited employees and residents to discuss how success should be defined before revising the system again.
sentences.ja: そのため窓口は制度を再修正する前に、成功をどう定義すべきか職員と住民に話し合ってもらった。

sentences.en: The discussion made clear that an evaluation system influences work even before a manager uses its results to make decisions.
sentences.ja: 議論によって、評価制度は管理職が結果を判断に使う前から仕事に影響することが明確になった。

sentences.en: People naturally pay attention to what their organizations reward, especially when their future opportunities depend on those rewards.
sentences.ja: 人々は組織が何を評価するかに注意を向けるものであり、将来の機会がそれに左右されるなら特にそうである。

sentences.en: A measurement can therefore change the activity it was originally designed to describe.
sentences.ja: したがって測定は、もともと記述するために作られた活動自体を変えることがある。

sentences.en: The experience did not show that targets and statistics should disappear from public administration.
sentences.ja: この経験は、目標や統計を行政からなくすべきだと示したわけではない。

sentences.en: It showed instead that decisions about what to measure are themselves decisions about what an institution chooses to value.
sentences.ja: むしろ何を測るかという決定自体が、制度が何に価値を置くかの決定だと示したのである。

sentences.en: Good measurements should reveal problems, support questions, and remain open to criticism from those affected by them.
sentences.ja: よい測定は問題を明らかにし、問いを支え、影響を受ける人々の批判に開かれているべきである。

sentences.en: They should not turn a complex public service into a contest in which only the easiest achievements are recognized.
sentences.ja: 複雑な公共サービスを、最も簡単な成果だけが認められる競争にしてはならない。

sentences.en: The most responsible institutions use indicators as tools for learning while keeping explanations, judgment, and opportunities for correction at the center.
sentences.ja: 最も責任ある制度は、説明、判断、訂正の機会を中心に保ちつつ、指標を学習の道具として使う。

sentences.en: Ultimately, a useful performance system asks not merely whether more work has been counted, but whether people's needs have actually been met.
sentences.ja: 結局、有益な業績制度は仕事が多く数えられたかだけでなく、人々の必要が実際に満たされたかを問う。

questions.prompt: What was rewarded under the initial system?
options: Resolving the largest number of requests each day.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第1段落の説明と一致するのは「Resolving the largest number of requests each day.」です。

questions.prompt: What initial result suggested success?
options: More completed cases and shorter queues.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第1段落の説明と一致するのは「More completed cases and shorter queues.」です。

questions.prompt: Which kind of case became less attractive?
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第1段落の説明と一致するのは「Complex cases requiring long conversations.」です。

questions.prompt: What is the central issue raised in paragraph one?
options: Whether faster service necessarily means better service.
How to remove all public offices.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第1段落の説明と一致するのは「Whether faster service necessarily means better service.」です。

questions.prompt: Why can numerical records be useful?
options: They always measure service quality fully.
They show delays and uneven workloads.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第2段落の説明と一致するのは「They show delays and uneven workloads.」です。

questions.prompt: What is the example of an informative number?
options: Counting the color of office chairs.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第2段落の説明と一致するのは「Counting unfinished applications.」です。

questions.prompt: What limitation do measurements have?
options: They are more complete than personal experience.
They record selected aspects, not everything that matters.
They cannot show workload at all.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第2段落の説明と一致するのは「They record selected aspects, not everything that matters.」です。

questions.prompt: How might narrowly focused targets affect workers?
options: They eliminate the need for staff judgment.
They make every applicant understand the rules.
They may discourage careful explanations to confused residents.
They guarantee more time for complex conversations.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第2段落の説明と一致するのは「They may discourage careful explanations to confused residents.」です。

questions.prompt: Why was the older resident's case difficult?
options: The resident wanted to buy a train ticket.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第3段落の説明と一致するのは「Several forms contained conflicting information.」です。

questions.prompt: What longer-term benefit did the employee's work provide?
options: Allowing the employee to close early.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第3段落の説明と一致するのは「Preventing repeated unnecessary visits.」です。

questions.prompt: How would the original system have evaluated that afternoon?
options: It would automatically count several cases.
It would look less productive than completing many easy cases.
It would reward the deepest discussion.
It would ignore the number of cases.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第3段落の説明と一致するのは「It would look less productive than completing many easy cases.」です。

questions.prompt: What knowledge may front-line workers have?
options: Practical information not easily visible to remote administrators.
The future results of all applications.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第3段落の説明と一致するのは「Practical information not easily visible to remote administrators.」です。

questions.prompt: What concern did critics raise?
options: Targets were too easy for all residents.
Workers might prioritize easy cases to improve scores.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第4段落の説明と一致するのは「Workers might prioritize easy cases to improve scores.」です。

questions.prompt: What did supporters fear if targets were removed?
options: Weak accountability and difficulty detecting poor service.
An increase in public trust without checks.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第4段落の説明と一致するのは「Weak accountability and difficulty detecting poor service.」です。

questions.prompt: What did the revised approach include?
options: Several indicators and discussions with employees.
One speed measure as the only standard.
A complete ban on public feedback.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第4段落の説明と一致するのは「Several indicators and discussions with employees.」です。

questions.prompt: What promise did managers make?
options: Every employee would receive the same pay.
No single indicator would decide a worker's evaluation.
Every difficult case would be rejected.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第4段落の説明と一致するのは「No single indicator would decide a worker's evaluation.」です。

questions.prompt: Why could satisfaction reports be misleading?
options: Every resident can judge legal accuracy.
Only dissatisfied people use public services.
Disappointed residents may report unhappiness despite fair explanations.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第5段落の説明と一致するのは「Disappointed residents may report unhappiness despite fair explanations.」です。

questions.prompt: What does a pleasant conversation fail to prove?
options: That the advice was complete and correct.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第5段落の説明と一致するのは「That the advice was complete and correct.」です。

questions.prompt: How did the office combine different evidence?
options: By refusing to review unusual cases.
With feedback, case reviews, privacy protections, and staff explanations.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第5段落の説明と一致するのは「With feedback, case reviews, privacy protections, and staff explanations.」です。

questions.prompt: What was the aim of the mixed evaluation?
options: Reveal strengths and limits rather than create a perfect score.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第5段落の説明と一致するのは「Reveal strengths and limits rather than create a perfect score.」です。

questions.prompt: Why did some employees change their behavior?
options: They had been ordered to stop helping.
Their organization rewarded speed more than careful problem solving.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第6段落の説明と一致するのは「Their organization rewarded speed more than careful problem solving.」です。

questions.prompt: Did the passage claim employees intended deception?
options: No, their actions responded to how the system rewarded work.
It said managers wanted to remove all records.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第6段落の説明と一致するのは「No, their actions responded to how the system rewarded work.」です。

questions.prompt: What did the office discuss before another revision?
options: How to eliminate all performance data.
How success in public service should be defined.
Which color should office walls have.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第6段落の説明と一致するのは「How success in public service should be defined.」です。

questions.prompt: What broader effect of measurement is identified?
options: Targets can alter the activity being measured.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第6段落の説明と一致するのは「Targets can alter the activity being measured.」です。

questions.prompt: What did the experience not prove?
options: That narrow metrics can be misleading.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第7段落の説明と一致するのは「That statistics should be eliminated.」です。

questions.prompt: Why are measurement choices also value choices?
options: They show which results the institution treats as important.
They make all work equally visible.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第7段落の説明と一致するのは「They show which results the institution treats as important.」です。

questions.prompt: How should strong institutions use indicators?
options: As a reason to ignore employee experience.
As tools for learning alongside judgment and correction.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第7段落の説明と一致するのは「As tools for learning alongside judgment and correction.」です。

questions.prompt: What does the conclusion ask performance systems to assess?
options: Whether queues can be eliminated entirely.
Whether people's actual needs are being met.
Only whether more cases were counted.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文第7段落の説明と一致するのは「Whether people's actual needs are being met.」です。

paraphrases.source: The new measurements therefore raised a question about whether greater efficiency always meant better public service.
paraphrases.rewrite: More cases completed does not automatically mean better public services.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 処理件数の増加と質は同じではないという問いです。

paraphrases.source: The challenge is to distinguish information that supports judgment from numbers that silently replace judgment.
paraphrases.rewrite: Data should assist professional decisions rather than take their place.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 数字は判断の代わりでなく判断を助けるものです。

paraphrases.source: It also demonstrated why people closest to the work sometimes possess knowledge that distant administrators cannot easily observe.
paraphrases.rewrite: Workers may understand difficulties that distant managers fail to see.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 現場の知識の価値を言い換えています。

paraphrases.source: Managers also promised that no single indicator would automatically determine an employee's evaluation.
paraphrases.rewrite: A single measure would no longer decide an employee's assessment.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 単一の指標で評価しないという方針です。

paraphrases.source: The aim was not to create a perfect score but to expose the strengths and limitations of each source of information.
paraphrases.rewrite: The aim was to understand the strengths and weaknesses of different information.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 情報源の利点と限界を知るという内容です。

paraphrases.source: A measurement can therefore change the activity it was originally designed to describe.
paraphrases.rewrite: Evaluating work can influence the work itself.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 測定が対象の活動を変えるという意味です。

paraphrases.source: Ultimately, a useful performance system asks not merely whether more work has been counted, but whether people's needs have actually been met.
paraphrases.rewrite: The important question is whether services actually satisfy people's needs.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 処理件数よりも必要の充足を重視しています。
